title: Introduce CUDA-graph handoff and lazy priming scheduler to reduce warmup stalls
author: Marisol Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see warmup stalls and intermittent regressions when CUDA-graph captures are created eagerly across mixed-shape workloads. Existing safeguards cause over-eager fallbacks or frequent replays when KV cache alignment drifts, leading to increased P50/P95 latency during warmup windows. This PR introduces a capture handoff model plus a "lazy priming" scheduler to reduce unnecessary captures and improve stability during dynamic batching.

What this change does (single-string summary): Adds a capture-handoff component that transfers capture ownership between worker groups when shape stability is detected, a profiling-guided lazy priming scheduler that only initiates priming captures when expected amortized win exceeds estimated capture cost, KV-cache alignment patches to reduce replay misses, and a conservative rollback hook to ensure safe fallback to interpreter kernels.

Key design points and rationale:
- Capture handoff: instead of globally forcing a capture when any worker sees a new shape, we introduce an ownership token that is granted to a worker group only after a short stability window. The owner is responsible for creating the capture and advertising it. Non-owners will continue to run optimized kernels until the capture is ready, avoiding mass invalidation. This reduces capture contention and the thundering-capture problem on bursty workloads.
- Lazy priming scheduler: uses light-weight sampling and recent-sequence profiling to estimate capture benefit (replay token savings + batching improvement) vs capture cost (kernel warmup + synchronization). Priming is scheduled only if expected net benefit > threshold. The threshold is tunable and defaults to a conservative value to prioritize safety.
- KV-cache alignment: when handoff occurs we perform an alignment probe to ensure KV pointers and offsets are compatible with the new capture; if alignment is off we perform targeted re-priming of the cache region instead of a full capture rollback. This reduces expensive full fallbacks.
- Rollback and safety: added a rollback fence that triggers a deterministic fallback path for in-flight requests when the capture fails or kernel mismatches are detected. The rollback path is deterministic and covered by new unit + integration tests.

Files changed (high level): src/runtime/capture/handoff_scheduler.cpp, src/runtime/priming/lazy_scheduler.rs, src/runtime/kv/aligner.cpp, src/runtime/replay/rollback_fence.cpp, tests/perf/cudagraph_handoff.yaml, docs/ops/cudagraph-handoff.md, examples/bench/handoff_microbench.py, build/ci/cudagraph-smoke.yml, rust-bindings/Cargo.toml, runtime/README.md, scripts/bench/collect_handoff_metrics.sh, e2e/fixtures/mixed_shape_sequences.json

Commit summary: single-squash merge of a 7-commit stack. Commits include: prototype scheduler and handoff token; alignment probe + KV patching; rollback fence + tests; perf harness and benchmark; docs + changelog; fixups for race in handoff token revocation; CI/bench integration.

Benchmarks: Microbench (internal perf lab) on T4/RTX6000 mixed-shape workload (random length 8-2048, 40% long tails): median latency during first 60s warmup decreased by ~9.8% vs baseline; P95 decreased by ~12.7%. Cold-start capture failures (captured->rollback) dropped from 6.4% to 1.1% in our traces. End-to-end token throughput improved by ~6% under continuous batching. Full benchmark logs attached to the CI artifact.

Testing: Unit tests added for handoff token lifecycle and kv alignment probe; integration tests simulate bursty mixed-shape traffic and assert no request amplification and consistent latency SLOs; e2e smoke in CI includes a deterministic seed to exercise rollback path. CI: all checks green after two reruns (first rerun needed due to flaky perf harness).

Docs & rollout: added ops doc (docs/ops/cudagraph-handoff.md) with recommended tuning knobs: stability_window_ms, priming_threshold, alignment_resample_count. Rollout plan: staged on Dedicated clusters with canary rollout to 10% of traffic, monitor warmup metrics and capture-failure counts, then 100% after 48h. Backout consists of disabling the handoff feature flag and reverting priming_threshold to +inf.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect handoff token revocation could leak stale captures. Mitigation: token revocation path has strong ordering fences and is covered by unit tests; added additional safety timeout that forces eviction after N seconds.
- Risk: misestimation by lazy scheduler could delay beneficial captures. Mitigation: conservative default threshold and a fast fallback path; we also ship an opt-in aggressive mode for high-throughput customers.
- Risk: KV alignment probe adds a small probe cost. Mitigation: probe limited to small header regions; microbench shows negligible steady-state overhead (<0.3%).

Related work and references: ENG-4821 (capture stability work), ENG-4890 (kv-cache regressions), internal notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/cudagraph-handoff-design.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration/perf tests added
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] Feature-flagged and rollout plan documented

Suggested reviewers: runtime team for correctness, perf team for benchmarks, SRE for rollout.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals from Ankit and Priya.

review_thread: Ankit Rao: Please add a test that exercises token revocation race. Added a small unit test in revocation_test.cpp and fixed an ordering bug.

Luca Moretti: Where do you store the ownership token? Make sure it doesn't become a global lock. Answer: token is sharded per-model+route and stored in the capture registry with expiry. Added comments and an LRU bound.
Priya Singh: Priming threshold tuning? Default seems conservative but documentable. Response: documented default and introduced runtime flag so SRE can tune per-deployment.
Perf CI: Initial perf run flaky, reran two times; second run shows consistent wins. CI artifact: perf/handoff-2026-02-01.zip
Approvals: Ankit Rao approved; Priya Singh approved with note to monitor capture-failure metrics for 48h.
release_notes: Add capture handoff and lazy priming scheduler to reduce CUDA-graph warmup regressions; improved KV alignment to reduce replay fallbacks; feature-flagged and disabled by default for Hosted API. See docs/ops/cudagraph-handoff.md for tuning.
